title: Mists Guide for Solo Players: Wisps, Brecilien and Safe Exits
author: Outpost
summary: How to find and pick a wisp, what each rarity changes, the difference between yellow and lethal Mists, how to earn Brecilien standing and unlock the city, and the habits that keep a solo player alive in there.

children: The Mists are small instanced zones built for solo players and duos. You enter through a wisp in the open world, farm mobs, chests and resources, and run into the occasional other player doing the same. They are the best place in Albion to learn solo PvP without a gank group on the other side of the screen, and the way to Brecilien.

title: How to Make Silver as a New Player in Albion Online
author: Outpost
summary: Safe ways to earn your first million silver with a fresh character: one gathering line, refining in the right city, selling loot properly and the mistakes that eat new players' savings.

children: Your first silver comes from boring, repeatable work in safe zones. Pick one method below, do it for a few evenings, and you will have enough for a real set, a transport mount and some breathing room. Skip the "fastest silver" videos that send day-one characters into red zones. Those methods work for people with a bankroll to lose.
Every crafter in Albion needs wood, ore, fiber, hide and stone, so raw resources always have buyers. Gathering also needs no combat spec and almost no gear.
Pick the resource that is most common near your starting city. Check the

Gather in blue and yellow zones. Nobody can take your gear there.
Gather the highest tier your tool and level allow, since each tier sells for more.
Stay with one line. Gathering levels are per resource, so splitting your time between ore and wood levels both slowly. When you can wear the matching gathering gear, the yield jump is large. The

Refine in the city that wants your resource
Each royal city gives a big return bonus for refining one resource:

Refining there gives back a larger share of your materials, and with focus the return passes 50%. Raw materials often sell for more in that city too, because refiners gather there. Run your numbers in the

Sell loot with orders, not at the first price
Mobs and chests drop gear you will not use. New players click "sell" and take whatever the top buy order pays. Sometimes that is right. Often it throws away a third of the value.

If the item is cheap or rarely trades, sell to the buy order and move on.
A sell order costs a 2.5% setup fee up front, and every sale pays tax: 4% with Premium, 8% without.

Carry a laborer journal on every trip

Empty journals fill with fame while you gather, craft or fight. A full journal sells to players who run laborers on their islands. Buy empty journals for the activity you do most and keep one in your bag. It costs almost nothing and turns every trip into a small extra sale.

Taking gear into a red or black zone that you cannot replace.
A player who kills you there takes everything you wear and carry.
A buy order (2.5%), a sell order (2.5%) and tax add up to at least 9% with Premium. A flip with a 5% gap loses money.
A price someone saw two days ago may be gone. Check how old a price is before you ride across the map for it.
Buying a hundred of something that sells five a day.
Volume matters more than the price tag.
Buying an expensive mount too early.
A cheap riding horse or ox does the job until you haul big loads.
Premium halves your sales tax, gives you daily focus for refining and crafting, and adds fame and gathering yield. You can buy it with silver through gold. Check the
page to see what Premium costs in silver on your server today. For a player who gathers and refines most evenings, it usually pays for itself.

Days 3 to 4: buy the next tool tier and the matching gathering cap and garb once you unlock them.

title: Gathering Guide: From T4 to T8 With Spec
author: Outpost
summary: The fastest route from your first T4 tool to T8 gathering in one resource: which line to pick, when to switch to gathering gear, what yield bonuses stack, how spec works per tier, and when to start gathering for profit instead of fame.

children: Gathering progression is a fame race, and the trick is gathering a lot of cheap resources fast instead of a few rare ones slowly. Most players who feel stuck at T6 are hunting T7 nodes. Gather plentiful lower-tier nodes in the matching gear and the tiers come much sooner.
Five lines exist: wood, ore, fiber, hide and stone. Each levels on its own, and gathering gear only boosts its own resource. Splitting your time early means levelling two lines at half speed.

title: The Depths Guide: Souls, Keys, Vaults and Getting Out Alive
author: Outpost
summary: How the Depths work for duos, trios and brave solo players: Orange Zone rules, entering in waves from the Antiquarian's Den, Souls and the two altars, the keys to the Treasure Vault on the last level, and the exits before the dungeon collapses.

children: The Depths are a three-level demon dungeon for groups of two or three, shared with other groups who want the same loot. They arrived with the Abyssal Depths update in 2025 and became one of the most popular fame and silver farms, partly because the PvP rules are gentle: you keep the gear you wear.

Wear the best set you can afford to repair. Losing it is off the table.
Carry only what you need into the dungeon, because the bag is what you risk.

title: Destiny Board Guide: Learning Points, Quick Learn and Fame Credits
author: Outpost
summary: How the Destiny Board levels you, what mastery and specialization nodes do, how Learning Points and Quick Learn speed up a node, what Fame Credits and re-spec are for, and where to spend your first points.

toc.title: Where to spend your first points

children: Albion has no character level. You get stronger by earning fame in what you do, and the

Fame goes to the node for the item you are using. Fighting with a Broadsword fills Broadsword and Sword Fighter; gathering T6 ore fills the T6 ore node.
The Radiant Wilds update made the board easier to read. Nodes you cannot progress yet are hidden by default and areas past your progress are dimmed. Use
to plan ahead, and look at the partial progress shown on connections to locked nodes.
Learning Points (LP) shortcut the fame a node needs. You get them from Premium (30 a day, granted once a day after maintenance, plus a one-time bonus with your first Premium) and from the shop.
Since mid-2025 you spend them through

. Switch Quick Learn on for a node and the fame you earn there is multiplied by five, with LP spent as that boosted fame comes in. The total LP cost of a node did not change. What changed is how you spend them: Quick Learn turns LP into progress only while you earn fame on that node.
That makes LP a speed-up for what you already do, so spend them on:
the gathering line you level every day,
crafting or refining specs that cut your focus costs.
Avoid spreading them across lines you might try later. Points sitting unspent cost nothing, and they keep.
Once a combat node is maxed, extra fame earned on it would be wasted.
catch it: with re-spec enabled on the board, fame from maxed nodes turns into credits, for a silver cost. Credits are bound to your character and cannot be traded.

You spend credits on any combat node that is already unlocked, which lets you level a new weapon quickly once your main is done. You can also convert mastery levels above the first into credits for silver. Rates and silver costs change with patches, so read the numbers on the board before you commit a large sum.

Put Quick Learn on the node you will earn the most fame in during that activity.
If you gather, a gathering line is the best first target; its unlocks are slow and the yield pays back.
If you fight, your main weapon's specialization adds IP to everything in that line.

title: Roads of Avalon Guide: Portals, Chests and Avalonian Dungeons
author: Outpost
summary: How the Roads of Avalon work for small groups: how portals and their capacities connect zones, what lives inside, how to scout and map a route home, guild hideouts, Avalonian Dungeons and the rules for logging out.

children: The Roads of Avalon are a maze of zones linked by temporary portals. Each portal has a player limit and a timer, so a road network that exists tonight is gone tomorrow. Small groups use the Roads for chests, high-tier resources and fights, and as a shortcut across the map. It is full-loot territory, and big groups cannot follow you through a small portal.
Avalonian portals open in the open world and connect to a Road zone. Inside, more portals link Road zones to each other and back out to the world.

Large portals are kept for the bigger "raid" regions, and group portals inside the Roads recharge between uses.
The tier of Road you reach depends on the zone type you came from.

Capacity is the safety feature. A seven-player portal stops a forty-player zerg from following you through.

Guilds can build hideouts in Avalonian Rest zones. A hideout gives a guild a bank and a home base deep in the network. Only guild members can place one, and keeping it shielded during battle time needs its power level kept up. A Roads hideout lets a guild farm a pocket of the network every night without the long ride in.

Avalonian Dungeons are the large-group elite dungeons, built for organised groups of 10 to 20 players at T6 to T8.4. They are among the hardest PvE in the game, with mechanics that wipe careless groups. You need a caller, a full roster with assigned roles and gear well above the entry requirement. Expect to learn the bosses with a guild or alliance that already runs them.
If you log out in the Roads, you come back where you first entered the network, and you take durability damage to your equipment and lose some stacked items. Plan to leave properly instead.

title: Zone Colors, PvP Flags and What You Lose When You Die

children: The colour of a zone on the map tells you what you can lose there. Learn the five rules once and most of Albion's risk becomes a choice you make on purpose. Most new players lose their first good set because they rode one zone further than they meant to.

The Royal Continent holds the blue, yellow and red zones around the six royal cities. The Outlands are all black. Orange rules apply in instanced content such as the Depths and the yellow-zone Ancient Lands.

You flag yourself hostile to fight other players. A player who loses is knocked down for a short time (90 seconds since mid-2025) and then gets up with their gear, minus durability. Yellow zones are where to practise PvP for the cost of repairs.

For a gatherer or hauler, red zones are the first real risk on the Royal Continent. Every road into Caerleon crosses them.

title: Group Dungeons Guide: Randomized, Static and Avalonian Runs
author: Outpost
summary: The kinds of group dungeon in Albion and what each is for: randomized group dungeons from maps and entrances, static dungeons on the world map, enchanted portals and the 20-player Avalonian Dungeons, with a party setup and the habits that make runs fast.

children: Group dungeons are where most players earn their combat fame once solo farming gets slow. Five players with a tank and a healer clear far faster than five soloists, and the loot is split among people who pulled their weight. There are three kinds, and they suit different groups.
Dungeon maps or random entrances in the world
Fixed entrances on the world map
Elite content, entered with organised large groups

toc.title: The centre and the Fire Drake

children: The Ancient Lands are a web of floating islands you enter through a portal, clear for loot, and leave before someone takes it from you. Every group starts alone, every route you open is visible to everyone, and the big rewards sit in the middle. Most of the skill is reading the map and knowing when to leave.

Portals show on the world map in small, medium and large sizes. The portal panel tells you the party size and how long the portal stays open. The game matches your party against groups of a similar size.
What you carry, including loot found inside. Your equipped gear is safe.

children: A good build answers one question first: what is it for? A solo dungeon set, a ZvZ healer and a gathering escape kit share almost nothing. Start from the activity and the rest of the choices get easy.

A short description saves the next reader a lot of guessing. Good notes cover:

You can type IP targets and ability notes. Outpost stores them as your notes. They are not verified combat stats and Outpost does not calculate them from the items, so readers should treat them as advice from the author.

title: How to Plan a Party Comp: Roles, Loadouts and Swaps
author: Outpost
summary: How to plan a party comp on Outpost for dungeons, Hellgates, Roads or ZvZ: pick a size, assign roles and players with substitutes, set each loadout and its swaps, and share the plan with your Team before the run.

toc.title: Example: a five-player group dungeon comp

children: A comp is the plan for a whole party: who plays what, in which gear, with which swaps. Writing it down before the content saves the first ten minutes of every run, and it stops the classic problem of three people turning up as DPS and nobody as tank.
and choose a size. The presets are 1, 2, 5, 7, 10 and 20, or type your own. A five-slot comp starts with a tank, a healer, a melee DPS and two ranged DPS, which you can change.

Shrinking the comp removes the members past the new size, and the editor asks before it does.
Select a slot to set its role: Tank, Healer, Melee DPS, Ranged DPS, or a custom role such as "Battlemount" or "Scout". Add the player who will fill it and a substitute for when they cannot.

Start with the slots the content cannot run without. In a group dungeon that is the tank and the healer. In ZvZ it is the callers' party and the supports. Fill DPS last; there are always more DPS players than anything else.
Give every slot its gear. Build it in place or copy one of your builds in. A copied build becomes the comp's own copy, so later changes to the original do not leak in.

for slots that change gear between fights, such as a second weapon for a boss or a different cape for PvP. Leave a note on any slot that needs one: the rotation, the call it follows, the potion to save.

Write the swap and note columns even when they feel obvious. The new player in slot 4 is the one who reads them.
Drag slots to reorder them. On a keyboard or touch screen, use the move buttons instead. If you move something by mistake,
puts it back. Most groups order by party: callers and tanks at the top, then healers, supports and DPS.
A Team shares comps, announcements, events and sign-ups among its current members. When someone leaves the Team, they lose access to what it shares.
Saving a comp does not post it to Discord. Share the link yourself, or export the comp as JSON or an image to paste elsewhere.
